correctness.rationale: Renormalized powered softmax probabilities satisfy \(p'(z)=\operatorname{softmax}(\alpha z)\). For \(V=\alpha W\), the PowerGrad head pseudo-gradient is \(\nabla_V\mathcal L(V,\theta)\), while its feature pseudo-gradient is \(\alpha^{-1}\nabla_\theta\mathcal L(V,\theta)\). These are exactly the two block derivatives of \(\Psi_\alpha=\alpha^{-1}\mathcal L(\alpha W,\theta)\). Multiplying the head update by \(\alpha\) gives the stated ordinary-CE block learning rates. Independent finite-difference and multi-step trajectory checks from the packaged verifier agree with every identity.

value.rationale: PowerGrad is motivated as a deliberate decoupling of forward and backward computation. Showing that its full plain-SGD field is actually conservative resolves a basic structural question about what objective the method follows. The exact \(1/lpha^2\) head/body rebalance is large at the exponents used to flatten gradients and supplies a concrete mechanism by which deep representation learning can change even though fixed-feature classification is only a rescaled ordinary-CE trajectory. This is a reusable optimizer interpretation, not a parameter renaming.
